text: The Emil J. Oberhoffer House is a historic residence located in Lakeville, Minnesota, United States, situated overlooking Orchard Lake. Emil Oberhoffer, who founded and served as the first conductor of the Minneapolis Symphony Orchestra, owned the home. The house was designed by Paul Haugen, an architect who worked for the firm Purcell and Elmslie, known for its Prairie School architectural style. Haugen began his career as an apprentice in Fargo, North Dakota, and after relocating to Minneapolis, he became influenced by Prairie School design principles. During a brief period of independence around 1913, Haugen designed this home as well as several other residences and a school in Burnsville. Later, the property was owned by the parents of golfer Patty Berg.
